title: ChroDrip - ProteinG
author: Alexandra Ehl
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.uwbexan
materials: Do you want to purify antibodies or sanitize your column? Please choose below.

steps.title: Prepare sample for loading
steps.instruction: Adjust sample pH to 7‑8 and NaCl to 150‑300 mM (add 1/11 volume 10× PBS), remove particulates by centrifugation or 0.45 µm filtration, then load onto the top of the column by gravity; for slow or weak‑binding antibodies collect the flow‑through and re‑apply it.

steps.title: Wash column after binding
steps.instruction: Add 5 column volumes of wash buffer and let it drain; repeat once (total 2 washes). Keep flow‑through and wash fractions for later analysis if desired. For higher purity repeat up to 5 times and optionally include up to 1 % Tween‑20 and/or up to 0.5 M NaCl in the wash buffer.

steps.title: Pre‑elution low‑volume step
steps.instruction: Add 0.75 column volumes of elution buffer to replace most of the wash buffer; this fraction does not contain the target protein and yields a more concentrated eluate.

steps.title: Elute target protein
steps.instruction: Place a clean tube under the column. Add three successive elution steps of 3 column volumes each, collecting each fraction in a separate tube and waiting for complete drainage between steps. For more concentrated eluates, perform eight elutions of 1 column volume each, collecting fractions separately. Identify the fraction(s) containing most protein and combine them.

steps.title: Neutralize eluate
steps.instruction: Add neutralization solution to the eluate at a rate of three drops per milliliter of eluate.

steps.title: Remove caps and initial wash
steps.instruction: Remove the bottom and top caps, add 5 column volumes of wash buffer (bed volume is indicated on the column). If re‑using a column, first drain the storage solution.

steps.title: Sequential column cleaning
steps.instruction: Wash the column successively with 5 column volumes elution buffer, then 5 column volumes wash buffer, then 5 column volumes deionized water. Add 10 column volumes of 20 % ethanol or wash buffer containing 0.05 % (w/v) sodium azide; let half of the buffer drain. Close the top lid and bottom stopper and store at room temperature or 4‑8 °C. For long‑term storage, dry the open column (top and bottom) in an oven at 80 °C for ≥2 h or overnight, ensure the bottom stopper is completely dry, attach the outlet, close the lid and store the closed column at room temperature.

steps.title: Post‑purification column wash
steps.instruction: After a purification, wash the column with 5 column volumes of elution buffer followed by 5 column volumes of wash buffer; let the buffer drain. If the column was previously stored, first let the buffer drain and then wash with 5 column volumes of wash buffer.

steps.title: Sanitization of column
steps.instruction: Add 5 column volumes of sanitization solution, let 1 column volume drain, then close the column with the top and bottom caps and incubate for 1 hour at room temperature.

steps.title: Drain sanitization and final rinse
steps.instruction: Drain the sanitization solution and wash the column with 10 column volumes of deionized water.

steps.title: Final storage buffer and hold
steps.instruction: Add approximately 5 column volumes of wash buffer containing 0.05 % (w/v) sodium azide; wait until half of the buffer has drained. Close the top lid and bottom stopper and store at room temperature or 4‑8 °C. Wait at least 12 hours before the next purification. For long‑term storage, dry the open column (top and bottom) in an oven at 80 °C for 2 hours or overnight, ensure the bottom stopper is completely dry, attach the outlet, close the lid and store the closed column at room temperature.
